claim: Engineered riblets will lift streamwise vortices away from the pipe surface, reducing the wetted surface area that vortices can act upon and decreasing drag by 6-9%
mechanism: The micro-ridges create anisotropic surface topology that lifts near-wall turbulent structures away from the pipe wall, similar to shark skin riblets lifting vortices away from the dermal denticles. This reduces the momentum transfer between the turbulent structures and the wall.
evidence: Shark skin riblets achieve 5-10% drag reduction in turbulent flow
Wind tunnel tests show riblets reduce drag when aligned with flow direction
assumptions: The riblet dimensions (height 50-200 μm, spacing 100-400 μm) are optimized for the pipe Reynolds number of 500,000
Flow remains predominantly aligned with riblets during normal operation
Manufacturing precision maintains consistent riblet geometry
expected_failure_modes: Manufacturing defects causing uneven riblet heights
Biofilm filling riblet valleys over time
novelty_rationale: This applies the specific vortex-lifting mechanism from shark skin to pipe flow, rather than generic surface roughness modifications
testability: Can be tested by measuring pressure drop in a pipe section with precisely manufactured riblets compared to smooth pipe under identical flow conditions
falsifier: If pressure measurements show no drag reduction or increased drag when riblets are aligned with flow direction
